name: Maximum-Parent Decomposition Depth and Feasible Ranks
statement: For every $k$, the sections $\mathcal P_k$ of maximum parents in $\mathcal D_k$ satisfy $\mathcal P_k\subseteq\mathcal D_k\cap\mathsf{MaxMin}$, $\mathcal P_k\subsetneq\mathcal P_{k+1}$, and $\bigcup_k\mathcal P_k=\mathcal P_D$. They are closed under nonempty sections, projections, and full reductions and are constant-coordinate invariant. Only $\mathcal P_0$ is complement closed. Moreover $\kappa(C)\le\lambda(C)$, with equality on maximum classes. When finite, feasible parent ranks at level $k$ are exactly all ranks at least $h_k(C)$; $h_k$ decreases with $k$ and stabilizes to $h_D(C)$ by $k\ge\max\{h_D(C)-1,0\}$.
proof: Section closure of each decomposition level gives the base inclusions and intrinsic-depth inequality; maximum classes are their own parents. Odd polygon complements give every strict level. Marks commute with projection, conditioning, and reduction, while the fixed-level constant-coordinate construction preserves the parent level. Complement closure holds at level zero and fails at every higher level by the complementary polygon pair. A nested successor construction raises parent rank one step without changing its level, giving the feasible-rank ray. Every rank-$r$ dismantlable class lies in $\mathcal D_{r-1}$, which gives stabilization at a least-rank dismantlable parent.
